record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Source of remote poles in channel Laplacian growth
record.original_question: For zero-surface-tension Saffman-Taylor/Laplacian growth in a channel represented by pole solutions, when one tries to make the zero-surface-tension dynamics reproduce the effects of vanishingly small surface tension by continually adding new remote poles, should the permanent source of those new poles be modeled as external noise, or as an infinite number of poles already present in the initial condition? In particular, which of those two mechanisms is the preferred explanation in the channel Laplacian-growth setting?

evidence.quote: Summing up, it is possible to tell, that for identity of the results with and without surface tension it is necessary to introduce a permanent source of the new remote poles: it may be either external noise or infinite number of poles in an initial condition. What from these methods is preferred it is a open question yet. In the case of flame front propagation it was shown [7], that external noise is necessary for an explanation of flame front velocity increase with the sizes of system: the infinite number of poles in an initial condition can not give this result. It is interesting to know, what is situation in the channel Laplacian growth.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider zero-surface-tension Saffman–Taylor (Laplacian) growth of a viscous fluid in a two-dimensional Hele–Shaw channel of finite width with periodic boundary conditions in the transverse direction. The interface separating the displaced fluid from the inviscid one is described, via a conformal map from a reference half-plane to the fluid domain, by a meromorphic function whose singularities are simple poles. Under the zero-surface-tension dynamics, each pole obeys a system of ODEs (the standard pole-decomposition equations for Laplacian growth in a channel), and the number of poles inside the analyticity domain is conserved.

It is known that the limit of vanishingly small surface tension does not coincide with the zero-surface-tension dynamics built from a finite collection of poles: to reproduce the small-surface-tension behavior using pole solutions one must continually supply new poles arriving from infinity ("remote poles") that subsequently migrate toward the interface. Two mechanisms have been proposed for the permanent source of these remote poles:

(A) external stochastic noise acting on the interface, which generates new poles at large distance at all times; or

(B) an infinite reservoir of poles present already in the initial condition, which one-by-one approach the interface as time evolves.

Question: In the channel Laplacian-growth setting, determine which of mechanisms (A) or (B) correctly reproduces the small-surface-tension limit of the dynamics. Equivalently, decide whether an appropriately chosen deterministic initial condition with infinitely many poles can reproduce all features of the vanishing-surface-tension limit (such as the dependence of characteristic interface velocities and finger-formation statistics on the channel width), or whether external noise is necessary.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for flame-front propagation (Kuramoto–Sivashinsky type pole dynamics) has been argued to require external noise, since an infinite pole reservoir in the initial condition cannot reproduce the observed growth of front velocity with system size. The corresponding question for channel Laplacian growth is explicitly posed as open, and no definitive resolution distinguishing the two mechanisms in that setting was located.

status_evidence.title: Pole solutions in flame front propagation and Saffman-Taylor problems
status_evidence.snippet: What from these methods is preferred it is an open question yet... It is interesting to know, what is situation in the channel Laplacian growth.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether external noise or an infinite initial set of poles is the correct mechanism in channel Laplacian growth is stated as open.
